props.name: interaction

props.name: padding
props.description: Space around the plot area, in pixels

props.name: palette
props.description: Series colors (defaults to the `--chart-series-1..8` CSS variables, then the theme colors)

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the chart

props.name: locale
props.description: Locale of the texts and numbers the chart writes (tooltip rows, compact units `k` / `万`, separators, month and weekday names of time axes)

props.name: labels
props.description: Overrides of the built-in texts of the `locale`

props.name: renderTooltip
props.description: React content of the tooltip (replaces the default content)

props.name: bins
props.description: Number of bins, or the rule choosing it: `sturges` (log2 n + 1, for small normal-ish samples), `freedman-diaconis` (bin width from the interquartile range, robust to outliers); `auto` uses Freedman-Diaconis and Sturges when the spread is zero

props.name: domain
props.description: Range covered by the bins (values outside are not counted); the data range by default

props.name: nice
props.description: Rounds the bin width to 1, 2 or 5 × 10^k and aligns the edges on it

examples.title: Fixed bins
examples.description: A domain and a count give round bins, one per 5 years here; formatBin writes the edges in the tooltip, typed arrays are binned without copies.

examples.title: Binning rules
examples.description: bins takes a count or a rule: auto (Freedman-Diaconis, robust to outliers), sturges (log2 n + 1) or a fixed number; the two groups of levels appear with enough bins.

examples.title: Cumulative share on click
examples.description: onPointClick gives the index of the clicked bin; binValues, called with the same options, returns its edges and counts to compute the share of employees at or below it. renderTooltip shows the count and share of each bin, and onPlotClick clears the selection.

examples.title: Comparing two samples
examples.description: histogramSeries builds the bars of a sample: with the same domain and count, two samples share their bins and sit side by side in a Chart.

examples.title: Latency distribution
examples.description: One million request latencies binned in a few milliseconds; quantiles gives the exact p50, p95 and p99, drawn as x reference lines.

examples.title: Live sliding window
examples.description: Wait times of the last 600 support calls, updated twice a second by a setInterval that is cleared on pause and unmount. A fixed domain, bin count and yAxis range keep the axes still while the distribution shifts, and the readout tracks the service level.

examples.title: Order values on a log scale
examples.description: Order values spanning three orders of magnitude are binned on their logarithm, so each bin covers the same ratio; formatBin and xAxis.format turn the edges back into dollars. Annotations mark the median, the p99 and the orders that qualify for free shipping.

examples.title: Process capability
examples.description: Diameters of machined parts against their tolerance: rect and line annotations mark the specification limits and the series prop draws the fitted normal curve over the bins. The readout computes the Cpk, and the switch shows the process once the tool is adjusted.

props.valueName: Name of the value in the tooltip
props.height: Height of the chart, the legend included: pixels or any CSS length
props.options: Other engine options (axes, legend, tooltip, palette, format…) merged with the element's own properties; property only
props.instance: The engine instance (minerva-design/charts/core), null until the element is rendered and connected

events.minerva-hover: The hovered (or keyboard-focused) points changed; detail: { x, xLabel, items }, null when nothing is hovered
events.minerva-point-click: A point or a bar was clicked; detail: { x, xLabel, items }
events.minerva-plot-click: The plot area was clicked where there is no point; detail: { x, y } in data coordinates
events.minerva-zoom: The user zoomed or panned; detail: { x, y } (the visible ranges)
events.minerva-renderer-change: The backend is ready, or fell back after a GPU loss; detail: { renderer }

methods.getView: Visible range, null before the engine is created
methods.getRenderer: Backend in use (webgpu, webgl2, webgl, canvas2d), null until ready
